name: Hong Kong Mahjong
description: Hong Kong Mahjong is a four-player Cantonese Mahjong variant that emphasizes practical hand building and fan-based scoring. The game uses the standard Mahjong tile set and straightforward meld structure, making it one of the most widely taught regional forms.

overview.description: Hong Kong Mahjong is a four-player Cantonese Mahjong variant that emphasizes practical hand building and fan-based scoring. The game uses the standard Mahjong tile set and straightforward meld structure, making it one of the most widely taught regional forms.

history.origins: Hong Kong Mahjong developed from earlier Chinese Mahjong forms and became the dominant urban Cantonese ruleset through the 20th century.
timeline: Early 20th century: Mahjong variants spread through southern China and Hong Kong.
Mid 20th century: Hong Kong table rules become widely standardized in local clubs.
Late 20th century onward: Rules documented and exported through diaspora communities.
history.cultural: Hong Kong Mahjong is a core social game in family gatherings, tea houses, and club play.
history.evolution: The variant retained classic draw-discard play while settling on approachable scoring expectations and common house-rule families.

setup.players: 4 players. Seats are assigned East, South, West, North.
setup.deck: Three suited tile groups 1-9, winds, dragons, flowers and seasons in a standard Mahjong set.
setup.dealing: Each player starts with 13 tiles; dealer (East) starts with 14 and discards first.

rules.objective: Complete a legal 14-tile Mahjong hand of four melds and one pair with sufficient scoring value.
rules.gameplay: Players draw one tile and discard one tile in turn. Discards may be claimed to form Chow, Pung, or Kong according to claim priority and position restrictions. A player wins by self-draw or discard claim when the hand is complete under table scoring requirements.
keyRules: East starts with 14 tiles; other players start with 13.
Each turn is draw one tile, then discard one tile.
Chow claims are limited to the player on the discarder's left; Pung and Kong can be claimed by any player.
Winning hand structure is four melds and one pair, with fan requirements determined by the table rule set.

strategy.basic: Prioritize efficient two-sided waits and avoid overcommitting to slow high-risk shapes.
strategy.intermediate: Track exposed tiles and likely dead waits to improve discard safety and completion speed.
strategy.advanced: Balance attack and defense based on seat position, hand value prospects, and visible opponent commitments.
tips: Keep flexible middle tiles early unless your hand has a clear value route.
Do not force expensive patterns when a clean, faster hand is available.
Watch claim tempo to infer opponent hand speed.

variations.name: Minimum Fan Tables
variations.description: Different clubs use different minimum fan thresholds to declare a winning hand.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Threshold is table configuration; no structural engine override required.

variations.name: Flowers and Seasons Enabled
variations.description: Flower and season bonuses are counted according to local table practice.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Bonus counting differs by table and is represented in scoring policy.

synthesis.shortDescription: Hong Kong Mahjong is a four-player Cantonese Mahjong variant emphasizing efficient hand construction, claim timing, and fan-based scoring.
